data.name: David M. Sabatini
data.lab: Sabatini Group, IOCB Prague (Prague, Czech Republic)
data.role: Identified mTOR (as RAFT1) in 1994. His lab then mapped much of the machinery around it: raptor and rictor at the core of mTORC1 and mTORC2, the Rag–Ragulator system that docks mTORC1 on the lysosome, and the sensors that detect leucine, arginine and SAM

data.name: Michael N. Hall
data.lab: Hall Lab, Biozentrum Basel (Basel, Switzerland)
data.role: Discovered TOR in yeast in 1991 and established it as a central controller of cell growth that responds to nutrients. His lab later showed that TOR works in two distinct complexes, TORC1 and TORC2, only one of which is blocked by rapamycin

data.name: Kun-Liang Guan
data.lab: Guan Lab, Westlake University (Hangzhou, Zhejiang, China)
data.role: Showed how growth-factor and energy signals reach mTORC1 through TSC2 and Rheb, and, in parallel with the Sabatini lab, that the Rag GTPases carry the amino-acid signal. His lab also found that AMPK and mTORC1 control autophagy by phosphorylating the kinase ULK1 at different sites

data.name: Brendan D. Manning
data.lab: Manning Lab, Harvard Chan School (Boston, Massachusetts, USA)
data.role: Was among the groups that in 2002 identified TSC2 as a direct target of Akt (MAN2002), linking insulin and PI3K signalling to mTORC1, and later found TBC1D7 as the third subunit of the TSC complex. His lab has shown how mTORC1 turns growth signals into the synthesis of lipids and nucleotides

data.name: John Blenis
data.lab: Blenis Lab, Weill Cornell Medicine (New York, New York, USA)
data.role: Showed early on that rapamycin blocks S6 kinase, then worked out how mTORC1 drives cell growth through its two main translation targets, S6K1 and 4E-BP1. His lab also found, in parallel with the Sabatini lab, that mTORC1 phosphorylates Grb10, a feedback brake on insulin signalling

data.name: Roberto Zoncu
data.lab: Zoncu Lab, UC Berkeley (Berkeley, California, USA)
data.role: Showed as a postdoc that mTORC1 senses amino acids from inside the lysosome, through the v-ATPase and Ragulator. His Berkeley lab has since mapped how the Rag GTPases and the folliculin complex switch mTORC1 on, and how lysosomal cholesterol feeds into the same system

data.name: Robert A. Saxton
data.lab: Saxton Lab, UC Berkeley (Berkeley, California, USA)
data.role: Solved, as a Sabatini-lab graduate student, the structures of the leucine sensor Sestrin2 and the arginine sensor CASTOR1, showing how each one grips its amino acid. He also co-wrote a widely cited 2017 review of mTOR signalling with David Sabatini

data.name: Do-Hyung Kim
data.lab: Kim Lab, University of Minnesota (Minneapolis, Minnesota, USA)
data.role: Co-discovered raptor, the defining partner of mTOR in mTORC1, and then mLST8 (GbetaL) as a Sabatini-lab postdoc. His Minnesota lab identified PRAS40 as an insulin-regulated link to mTORC1 and studies how mTORC1 controls autophagy

data.name: Dos D. Sarbassov
data.lab: Faculty profile, Nazarbayev University (Astana, Kazakhstan)
data.role: Discovered rictor as a Sabatini-lab postdoc, in parallel with Michael Hall's lab, defining mTOR Complex 2, and showed that this complex is the long-sought kinase that phosphorylates Akt on serine 473. He also found that prolonged rapamycin treatment can block mTORC2 assembly

data.name: Yasemin Sancak
data.lab: Sancak Lab, University of Washington (Seattle, Washington, USA)
data.role: Showed as a Sabatini-lab graduate student, in parallel with Kun-Liang Guan's lab, that the Rag GTPases relay amino-acid signals to mTORC1, and that Ragulator anchors them to the lysosome where mTORC1 is switched on. She also identified PRAS40 as an insulin-regulated inhibitor of mTORC1

data.name: Randy Strong
data.lab: Faculty profile, Barshop Institute (San Antonio, Texas, USA)
data.role: Leads the San Antonio site of the NIA Interventions Testing Program, which tests each compound in parallel at three sites under one shared protocol. He first-authored the program's reports on resveratrol and other supplements (2012) and on rapamycin combined with acarbose (2022)

data.name: Richard A. Miller
data.lab: Miller Lab, University of Michigan (Ann Arbor, Michigan, USA)
data.role: Leads the University of Michigan site of the NIA Interventions Testing Program. His papers showed that rapamycin extends mouse lifespan when started in middle age, and that the size of the benefit depends on dose and differs between males and females

data.name: David E. Harrison
data.lab: Faculty profile, The Jackson Laboratory (Bar Harbor, Maine, USA)
data.role: Led the Jackson Laboratory site of the NIA Interventions Testing Program. His 2009 Nature paper showed that rapamycin extends the lifespan of genetically diverse mice even when feeding starts at 20 months of age, which the authors described as the first pharmacological extension of lifespan in both sexes of a mammal

data.name: Carson C. Thoreen
data.lab: Thoreen Lab, Yale (New Haven, Connecticut, USA)
data.role: Used Torin1, one of the first ATP-competitive mTOR inhibitors, to reveal functions of mTORC1 that rapamycin cannot block. He then showed that mTORC1 controls translation of mRNAs for the protein-making machinery mainly through the 4E-BP proteins

data.name: Lynne Chantranupong
data.lab: Chantranupong Lab, Boston University (Boston, Massachusetts, USA)
data.role: Showed as a Sabatini-lab graduate student that the Sestrins act through GATOR2 to regulate amino-acid signalling to mTORC1. She then discovered the CASTOR proteins, the cell's arginine sensors for the pathway

data.name: Ken Inoki
data.lab: Inoki Lab, U. Michigan LSI (Ann Arbor, Michigan, USA)
data.role: Showed as a postdoc in Kun-Liang Guan's lab that Akt switches off TSC2, that TSC2 is the off-switch (GAP) for the small GTPase Rheb, and that AMPK and GSK3 feed energy and Wnt signals into the same brake. His Michigan lab studies mTOR signalling in metabolism and kidney disease

data.name: Siraj M. Ali
data.lab: Translational Medicine, Lunit (Seoul, South Korea)
data.role: Worked in the Sabatini lab on the papers that discovered raptor, mLST8 and rictor, and on the finding that the rictor-mTOR complex phosphorylates Akt. He later moved into cancer genomics and clinical diagnostics

data.name: Hediye Erdjument-Bromage
data.lab: Mass Spectrometry Core, NYU Langone (New York, New York, USA)
data.role: Ran the mass-spectrometry analyses in Paul Tempst's lab at Memorial Sloan Kettering that identified the unknown proteins in the raptor, mLST8 and rictor purifications, and contributed the same approach to work on how ERK inactivates TSC2

data.name: Paul Tempst
data.lab: Tempst Lab, Sloan Kettering Institute (New York, New York, USA)
data.role: Developed mass-spectrometry methods for identifying proteins from tiny samples, and led the Memorial Sloan Kettering proteomics laboratory that identified the unknown partners of mTOR in the raptor, mLST8 and rictor purifications

data.name: Reuben J. Shaw
data.lab: Shaw Lab, Salk Institute (La Jolla, California, USA)
data.role: Showed, in parallel with two other groups, that the tumour suppressor LKB1 directly activates AMPK, and that AMPK brakes mTORC1 by phosphorylating raptor. His Salk lab also linked AMPK to autophagy through ULK1 and helped explain how metformin acts in the liver

data.name: Rachel L. Wolfson
data.lab: Wolfson Lab, Harvard Medical School (Boston, Massachusetts, USA)
data.role: Identified Sestrin2 as the direct leucine sensor of the mTORC1 pathway as a Sabatini-lab MD-PhD student. She also co-discovered KICSTOR, the complex that recruits GATOR1 to the lysosome

data.name: Dudley W. Lamming
data.lab: Lamming Lab, UW-Madison (Madison, Wisconsin, USA)
data.role: Showed as a postdoc that rapamycin's harm to glucose metabolism comes largely from its effect on mTORC2, while the lifespan benefit tracks mTORC1. His Wisconsin lab studies intermittent rapamycin dosing and how restricting dietary protein or single amino acids affects metabolism and ageing

data.name: Liron Bar-Peled
data.lab: Bar-Peled Lab, MGH & Harvard (Boston, Massachusetts, USA)
data.role: Showed as a Sabatini-lab graduate student that Ragulator switches the Rag GTPases on, acting as their GEF. He also discovered GATOR1 and GATOR2; GATOR1 switches the Rags off and its genes are mutated in some cancers

data.name: Lewis C. Cantley
data.lab: Cantley Lab, Dana-Farber (Boston, Massachusetts, USA)
data.role: Co-discovered PI3K, the pathway that feeds into mTOR from growth factors

data.name: David A. Guertin
data.lab: Guertin Lab, UMass Chan (Worcester, Massachusetts, USA)
data.role: Built the mouse genetics that defined mTORC2's biological roles

data.name: Matt Kaeberlein
data.lab: Dog Aging Institute (Seattle, Washington, USA)
data.role: Extended TOR/aging research from yeast to mice to pet dogs

data.name: Andrea Ballabio
data.lab: Ballabio Lab, TIGEM (Naples, Italy)
data.role: Discovered that the transcription factor TFEB is a master switch for building lysosomes (SAR2009) and for autophagy. His lab was one of the groups that showed in 2012 that mTORC1 keeps TFEB out of the nucleus from the lysosome surface, and later (2020) that constitutive TFEB activation drives the kidney disease of Birt-Hogg-Dubé syndrome

data.name: Estela Jacinto
data.lab: Jacinto Lab, Rutgers RWJMS (Piscataway, New Jersey, USA)
data.role: Co-discovered mammalian mTORC2 as a postdoc in Michael Hall's lab, showing that it controls the actin cytoskeleton and is insensitive to rapamycin. Her Rutgers lab, with Bing Su's group, was among those that found SIN1 holds mTORC2 together and studies how both mTOR complexes control metabolism

data.name: Robert R. Latek
data.lab: Sabatini Lab, Whitehead Institute for Biomedical Research (Cambridge, Massachusetts, USA)
data.role: Bioinformatics scientist at the Whitehead Institute who worked on the Sabatini-lab papers that described raptor, mLST8 (GbetaL) and rictor (raptor and rictor were reported in parallel by other labs), the core partners of mTOR in its two complexes

data.name: Joan B. Mannick
data.lab: Profile, Altos Labs (Redwood City, California, USA)
data.role: Ran early clinical trials of low-dose mTOR inhibitors in older adults, which improved their response to flu vaccination and, in a phase 2a trial, their rate of self-reported infections; a larger phase 3 trial of RTB101 (2021) did not confirm a reduction in respiratory illness. She led this work first at Novartis and then at resTORbio

data.name: Arlan Richardson
data.lab: Faculty profile, OU Health (Oklahoma City, Oklahoma, USA)
data.role: Studies how rapamycin slows ageing in mice, including the broad changes it causes in the liver, and co-authored early studies showing that rapamycin protects memory in Alzheimer's-model mice

data.name: Davide Ruggero
data.lab: Ruggero Lab, UCSF (San Francisco, California, USA)
data.role: Showed that oncogenic mTOR signalling reprograms which mRNAs are translated, and that tumours become addicted to this through the 4E-BP–eIF4E axis. His UCSF lab found that mTOR-driven translation of a specific set of mRNAs promotes prostate cancer invasion and metastasis

data.name: George Thomas
data.lab: Metabolism and Cancer group, IDIBELL (L'Hospitalet de Llobregat, Spain)
data.role: Purified and cloned S6K1, the kinase that became the classic readout of mTORC1 activity. His lab later showed that mice lacking S6K1 resist diet-induced obesity, and that amino acids signal to mTORC1 through the lipid kinase hVps34 (GUL2008)

data.name: Alexander J. Valvezan
data.lab: Valvezan Lab, Rutgers CABM (Piscataway, New Jersey, USA)
data.role: Showed as a Manning-lab postdoc that mTORC1 matches nucleotide production to demand, creating a weak point that can be targeted in tumours with TSC loss. His Rutgers lab found that mTORC1 activity rises and falls through the cell cycle and helps drive entry into mitosis

data.name: Joseph Avruch
data.lab: Profile, MGH Research Institute (Boston, Massachusetts, USA)
data.role: Showed in 1998 that amino acids, not only insulin, are needed for mTOR to activate S6K1 and 4E-BP1. His Massachusetts General Hospital group, with Kazuyoshi Yonezawa's lab in Kobe, then co-discovered raptor in 2002 and found that Rheb binds mTOR directly

data.name: Christian C. Dibble
data.lab: Dibble Lab, BIDMC & Harvard (Boston, Massachusetts, USA)
data.role: Identified TBC1D7 as the third subunit of the TSC complex that controls mTORC1, as a Manning-lab graduate student. His lab at Beth Israel Deaconess studies how PI3K signalling and nutrient supply are integrated to control mTORC1 and cell metabolism

data.name: Nathanael S. Gray
data.lab: Gray Lab, Stanford (Stanford, California, USA)
data.role: Medicinal chemist whose lab designed Torin1, an ATP-competitive mTOR inhibitor that blocks functions of mTORC1 that rapamycin misses. His lab is also known for covalent kinase inhibitors and targeted protein degraders

data.name: Seong A. Kang
data.lab: Sabatini Lab, Whitehead Institute for Biomedical Research (Cambridge, Massachusetts, USA)
data.role: Contributed to the Sabatini-lab studies that identified PRAS40 and DEPTOR, two of the cell's own mTOR inhibitors, and to the first characterisation of the mTOR inhibitor Torin1

data.name: Timothy R. Peterson
data.lab: Profile, WashU Musculoskeletal Center (St. Louis, Missouri, USA)
data.role: Discovered DEPTOR, an inhibitor that binds mTOR in both complexes and is overexpressed in some multiple myelomas. He also showed that mTORC1 controls fat synthesis by regulating where the enzyme lipin 1 sits in the cell, and through it the SREBP pathway

data.name: Jonathan D. Powell
data.lab: Profile, Calico Life Sciences (South San Francisco, California, USA)
data.role: Showed that T cells lacking mTOR become regulatory T cells instead of effector cells, and that mTORC1 and mTORC2 each steer a different type of helper T cell

data.name: Kuang Shen
data.lab: Shen Lab, UMass Chan (Worcester, Massachusetts, USA)
data.role: Solved, as a Sabatini-lab postdoc, cryo-EM structures of GATOR1 and of the FLCN–FNIP2–Rag–Ragulator complex, two switches that set mTORC1 activity. His UMass Chan lab studies the structural basis of nutrient sensing

data.name: Kazuyoshi Yonezawa
data.lab: Researcher record (KAKEN), Kobe University (Kobe, Japan)
data.role: Led the Kobe University group that co-discovered raptor in 2002, in parallel with the Sabatini lab. His team then showed that raptor binds mTOR's substrates through their TOS motif and that PRAS40 is itself an mTORC1 substrate

data.name: Andrew R. Tee
data.lab: Faculty profile, Cardiff University (Cardiff, Wales, United Kingdom)
data.role: First author of one of several 2003 papers showing that the TSC1–TSC2 complex acts as a GTPase-activating protein for Rheb

data.name: Sue Menon
data.lab: Profile, Manning Lab (Harvard Chan) (Boston, Massachusetts, USA)
data.role: Showed insulin controls mTORC1 by moving the TSC complex on and off the lysosome

data.name: Jay N. Joshi
data.lab: Valvezan Lab, Rutgers (Piscataway, New Jersey, USA)
data.role: Showed mTORC1 activity itself rises and falls across the cell cycle, not just in response to nutrients

data.name: Shuyu Wang
data.lab: Manoli Lab, UCSF (San Francisco, California, USA)
data.role: Co-discovered SLC38A9 as a Sabatini-lab MD-PhD student, a lysosomal amino-acid transporter that signals arginine sufficiency to mTORC1

data.name: Anne Brunet
data.lab: Brunet Lab, Stanford (Stanford, California, USA)
data.role: Showed that Akt directly phosphorylates and controls FOXO, the transcription-factor switch linking insulin/IGF-1 signaling to lifespan

data.name: Miriam Ginzberg
data.lab: Kafri Lab, SickKids (Toronto, Ontario, Canada)
data.role: Helped build a way to read a signal's history from still images of fixed cells, then used it to catch mTORC1's fingerprint on Akt

data.name: Ran Kafri
data.lab: Kafri Lab, SickKids (Toronto, Ontario, Canada)
data.role: Studies how mTORC1 sets and enforces a target size for cells

data.name: Lingjun Lu
data.lab: Androulakis Group, Rutgers (Piscataway, New Jersey, USA)
data.role: Built a computational model treating mTORC1 as a rhythm set by meal timing, not a fixed level

data.name: Ioannis P. Androulakis
data.lab: Androulakis Group, Rutgers (Piscataway, New Jersey, USA)
data.role: Models how circadian rhythm and nutrient-sensing pathways like mTORC1 stay synchronized

data.name: Ruizhao Wang
data.lab: Piatkevich Lab, Westlake University (Hangzhou, Zhejiang, China)
data.role: Built FPTT, fluorescent 'ticker tapes' that record several signalling pathways in living cells over days, and used its mTOR version to follow mTOR activity oscillating through the cell cycle

data.name: Jian Jiang
data.lab: Xie Lab (Biosystems Engineering Laboratory), Westlake University (Hangzhou, Zhejiang, China)
data.role: Co-developed FPTT, fluorescent 'ticker tapes' that record several signalling pathways in living cells over days, including an mTOR recorder that tracked mTOR activity oscillating through the cell cycle

data.name: Stuart L. Schreiber
data.lab: Faculty profile, Harvard University (Cambridge, Massachusetts, USA)
data.role: Co-discovered mTOR in 1994 (his group called it FRAP) as the mammalian target of the FKBP12–rapamycin complex, and helped found chemical biology as a field

data.name: Nahum Sonenberg
data.lab: Faculty profile, McGill University (Montreal, Quebec, Canada)
data.role: Co-discovered the mRNA cap-binding protein eIF4E and the 4E-BP proteins that restrain it, and showed how mTOR releases this brake to control protein synthesis

data.name: Dario R. Alessi
data.lab: Principal investigator page, MRC Protein Phosphorylation Unit, University of Dundee (Dundee, Scotland, United Kingdom)
data.role: Co-discovered PDK1, the master kinase that switches on Akt and related AGC kinases, and showed that mTORC2 activates the kinase SGK1

data.name: Nikola P. Pavletich
data.lab: Pavletich Lab, Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center (New York, New York, USA)
data.role: Solved the crystal structure of the mTOR kinase, revealing the FRB domain as a gatekeeper of its active site, and later showed how RHEB switches mTORC1 on and PRAS40 blocks it

data.name: J. Wade Harper
data.lab: Harper Lab, Harvard Medical School (Boston, Massachusetts, USA)
data.role: Co-discovered the F-box motif that links substrates to SCF ubiquitin ligases, and co-leads with Steven Gygi the BioPlex protein-interaction map, which contributed to the discoveries of the CASTOR and SAMTOR nutrient sensors

data.name: Steven P. Gygi
data.lab: Gygi Lab, Harvard Medical School (Boston, Massachusetts, USA)
data.role: Mass-spectrometry scientist whose Harvard lab builds large-scale proteomics methods, including the BioPlex human protein-interaction map, and contributed proteomics to the discoveries of the CASTOR and SAMTOR nutrient sensors

data.name: Kevan M. Shokat
data.lab: Faculty profile, UCSF (San Francisco, California, USA)
data.role: Co-developed the ATP-competitive 'TORKinib' mTOR inhibitors that block both mTORC1 and mTORC2, and later, with Neal Rosen's lab at Memorial Sloan Kettering, RapaLink-1, a third-generation inhibitor that overcomes mTOR resistance mutations

data.name: Pier Paolo Pandolfi
data.lab: Personal website (Reno, Nevada, USA)
data.role: Showed that ERK directly phosphorylates and inactivates TSC2, wiring Ras/MAPK signalling into mTORC1 control, and that blocking mTORC1 in patients' tumours triggers a feedback rise in MAPK signalling

data.name: Brian K. Kennedy
data.lab: Faculty profile, National University of Singapore (Singapore)
data.role: Showed with Matt Kaeberlein that reducing TOR or Sch9 signalling extends yeast lifespan in the same way as dietary restriction, and has since championed mTOR as a target for slowing human ageing

data.name: Linda Partridge
data.lab: Emerita profile, Max Planck Institute for Biology of Ageing (Cologne, North Rhine-Westphalia, Germany)
data.role: Showed that rapamycin extends fruit-fly lifespan through TORC1, via autophagy and reduced protein synthesis, and that it adds benefit even on top of dietary restriction

data.name: John J. Kopchick
data.lab: Institute for Molecular Medicine and Aging, Ohio University (formerly Edison Biotechnology Institute) (Athens, Ohio, USA)
data.role: Discovered the growth hormone receptor antagonist that became the acromegaly drug pegvisomant (Somavert), and studies how blocking growth hormone signalling extends lifespan in mice

data.name: Darlene E. Berryman
data.lab: Institute for Molecular Medicine and Aging, Ohio University Heritage College of Osteopathic Medicine (Athens, Ohio, USA)
data.role: Showed that growth hormone reshapes fat tissue in a depot-specific way that links body composition to metabolic aging

data.name: Edward O. List
data.lab: Institute for Molecular Medicine and Aging, Ohio University Heritage College of Osteopathic Medicine (Athens, Ohio, USA)
data.role: Carries out mouse studies, in John Kopchick's group, on how disrupting growth hormone receptor signaling extends mammalian lifespan

data.name: Alejo Efeyan
data.lab: Metabolism and Cell Signalling Group, Spanish National Cancer Research Centre (CNIO) (Madrid, Spain)
data.role: Showed that the Rag GTPases, which relay amino-acid signals to mTORC1, are a life-or-death switch for newborn mice surviving the fast before their first feeding

data.name: Sue C. Bodine
data.lab: Aging & Metabolism Research Program, Oklahoma Medical Research Foundation (OMRF) (Oklahoma City, Oklahoma, USA)
data.role: Showed that turning on the Akt-mTOR pathway is enough, by itself, to make skeletal muscle grow and to stop it from wasting away

data.name: Xiaomeng Long
data.lab: Avruch Lab, Massachusetts General Hospital / Harvard Medical School (Boston, Massachusetts, USA)
data.role: Discovered that Rheb binds directly to the mTOR kinase domain and switches it on

data.name: Kenta Hara
data.lab: Department of Diabetes & Endocrinology, Kita Harima Medical Center (Ono, Hyogo, Japan)
data.role: Showed in 1998 that amino acids are needed for mTOR to activate S6K1 and 4E-BP1, and as first author co-discovered raptor in 2002

data.name: Noriko Oshiro-Rapley
data.lab: Xavier Lab, MGH Center for Computational & Integrative Biology / Broad Institute (Boston, Massachusetts, USA)
data.role: In one of several 2007 studies, identified PRAS40 as a raptor-bound mTORC1 substrate that gates access to mTORC1's other substrates

data.name: Grace Y. Liu
data.lab: Vance Lab, University of California, Berkeley (Berkeley, California, USA)
data.role: Wrote with David Sabatini a major 2020 review of mTOR in nutrition, growth and ageing, and in the Sabatini lab studied how mTORC1 senses nutrients such as serine

data.name: Kendall J. Condon
data.lab: PhD (Sabatini lab), MIT Department of Biology (Cambridge, Massachusetts, USA)
data.role: Ran genome-wide CRISPR screens revealing how mitochondrial stress signals to mTORC1

data.name: Sonia M. Scaria
data.lab: Tward Lab alumni record, UCSF Otolaryngology–Head and Neck Surgery (San Francisco, California, USA)
data.role: Contributed, as an MIT undergraduate in the Sabatini lab, to the discovery of CASTOR1 as the arginine sensor and SAMTOR as the SAM sensor of the mTORC1 pathway

data.name: Mathieu Laplante
data.lab: Institut universitaire de cardiologie et de pneumologie de Québec – Université Laval (Quebec City, Quebec, Canada)
data.role: Co-wrote with David Sabatini one of the field's most cited reviews of mTOR in growth and disease, and his Laval lab studies how mTORC1 and DEPTOR control fat tissue and metabolism

data.name: J. Silvio Gutkind
data.lab: Gutkind Lab, UC San Diego Moores Cancer Center (La Jolla, California, USA)
data.role: Showed that persistent mTOR activation exhausts epidermal stem cells and accelerates skin ageing, and targets PI3K–mTOR signalling in head-and-neck cancer, including to make tumours respond to immunotherapy

data.name: Matthew R. Janes
data.lab: Wellspring Biosciences, Inc. (San Diego, California, USA)
data.role: Showed, as first author in David Fruman's lab, that a dual TORC1/2 kinase inhibitor kills leukemia cells with much weaker effects on normal lymphocytes than rapamycin

data.name: Andrew C. Hsieh
data.lab: Hsieh Lab, Fred Hutchinson Cancer Center (Seattle, Washington, USA)
data.role: Showed, as first author in Davide Ruggero's lab, that oncogenic mTOR drives cancer metastasis by selectively translating a specific pro-invasion mRNA program

data.name: Mikhail V. Blagosklonny
data.lab: In memoriam / Aging (Aging-US) editor profile (Buffalo, New York, USA)
data.role: Proposed the hyperfunction theory of ageing: TOR signalling that builds a young body never fully switches off, and drives its ageing instead

data.name: Gerta Hoxhaj
data.lab: Children's Medical Center Research Institute (CRI), UT Southwestern Medical Center (Dallas, Texas, USA)
data.role: Studies how growth signalling through PI3K, AKT and mTOR rewires cell metabolism; as a Manning-lab postdoc she co-authored work on how metformin inhibits mTORC1 in the liver

data.name: Carmine Settembre
data.lab: Settembre Lab, TIGEM (Telethon Institute of Genetics and Medicine) (Naples, Italy)
data.role: Showed, as first author in Andrea Ballabio's lab, that TFEB drives autophagy as well as lysosome production, and, in parallel with other groups, that mTORC1 phosphorylates TFEB at the lysosome to keep this program switched off when nutrients are plentiful

data.name: Michael D. Frost
data.lab: Minnesota Epilepsy Group (St. Paul, Minnesota, USA)
data.role: Co-investigator on the EXIST-1 and EXIST-2 trials showing that the mTOR inhibitor everolimus shrinks tuberous sclerosis tumours in the brain and kidney

data.name: John J. Bissler
data.lab: St. Jude Children's Research Hospital (Memphis, Tennessee, USA)
data.role: Led the first clinical trial showing that the mTOR inhibitor sirolimus shrinks kidney angiomyolipomas in tuberous sclerosis, and the EXIST-2 trial of everolimus for the same tumours

data.name: David N. Franz
data.lab: Tuberous Sclerosis Clinic, Cincinnati Children's Hospital Medical Center (Cincinnati, Ohio, USA)
data.role: Led the EXIST-1 trial showing that the mTOR inhibitor everolimus shrinks the brain tumours (SEGAs) of tuberous sclerosis, and helped run the first sirolimus trial for its kidney tumours

data.name: Pankaj Kapahi
data.lab: Kapahi Lab, Buck Institute for Research on Aging (Novato, California, USA)
data.role: Showed that reducing TOR signalling extends fruit-fly lifespan, and that the translation repressor 4E-BP is needed for dietary restriction to extend it

data.name: Vanessa S. Rodrik-Outmezguine
data.lab: Clinical Biomarker Development, Loxo Oncology at Eli Lilly and Company (formerly Rosen Lab, Memorial Sloan Kettering) (Stamford, Connecticut, USA)
data.role: Showed that tumours reactivate AKT after mTOR kinase inhibition, and that the third-generation inhibitor RapaLink-1 overcomes mTOR resistance mutations

data.name: Neal Rosen
data.lab: Rosen Lab (Member Emeritus), Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center (New York, New York, USA)
data.role: Showed that blocking mTORC1 releases a feedback brake on receptor tyrosine kinases and AKT, explaining how tumours escape mTOR and PI3K inhibitors and shaping how these drugs are combined in the clinic

data.name: Brian C. Grabiner
data.lab: Sabatini Lab, Whitehead Institute / MIT (HHMI) (Cambridge, Massachusetts, USA)
data.role: Catalogued cancer-associated MTOR mutations and showed that many of them hyperactivate the kinase and can predict sensitivity to rapamycin; he also contributed to the discovery of GATOR1

data.name: Yakir Guri
data.lab: Hall Lab, Biozentrum, University of Basel (Basel, Switzerland)
data.role: Showed mTORC2 drives liver cancer by rewiring lipid and sphingolipid synthesis

data.name: Robbie Loewith
data.lab: Loewith Lab, University of Geneva (Geneva, Switzerland)
data.role: Showed, as first author in Michael Hall's lab, that yeast TOR exists as two distinct complexes, the basis of the TORC1/TORC2 framework

data.name: Haijuan Yang
data.lab: Pavletich Lab, Structural Biology Program, Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center (New York, New York, USA)
data.role: Solved, as first author in the Pavletich lab, the crystal structure of the mTOR kinase and the structure of mTORC1 activated by RHEB

data.name: Chong Chen
data.lab: The Chen-Liu Lab, State Key Laboratory of Biotherapy, West China Hospital, Sichuan University (Chengdu, Sichuan, China)
data.role: Showed that blood stem cells need TSC to keep mTOR in check in order to stay dormant and self-renew, and that rapamycin restores the function of aged blood stem cells in mice

data.name: Pan Zheng
data.lab: OncoC4, Inc. (Rockville, Maryland, USA)
data.role: Showed as senior author that blood stem cells need TSC to keep mTOR in check in order to stay dormant, and that rapamycin restores the function of aged blood stem cells in mice

data.name: Benoit Viollet
data.lab: Institut Cochin (INSERM/CNRS/Université Paris Cité) (Paris, France)
data.role: Showed that metformin still lowers liver glucose production without AMPK or LKB1, pointing instead to a drop in cellular energy charge

data.name: Joungmok Kim
data.lab: Kyung Hee University (Seoul, South Korea)
data.role: Showed as a Guan-lab postdoc that AMPK and mTORC1 control autophagy by phosphorylating ULK1 at different sites, with mTORC1's mark on Ser757 blocking activation by AMPK

data.name: Constantinos Demetriades
data.lab: Demetriades Lab, European Research Institute for the Biology of Ageing (ERIBA), UMCG (Groningen, Netherlands)
data.role: Showed as a postdoc in Aurelio Teleman's lab that starvation and other stresses pull TSC2 to the lysosome to switch mTORC1 off.
